h1: Banyan Residence Rayong — a quiet serviced apartment with roomy suites, a separate sitting area, and free parking
intro: Picture this: you turn into a quiet lane in Noen Phra in the evening, park easily in the private lot out front, and walk into a suite with a sitting area set apart from the bed. You drop your bags, open the fridge for a cold drink, and settle on the balcony where you can barely hear traffic — Banyan Residence is a 3-star serviced apartment in Mueang Rayong, tucked into a quiet residential neighborhood about 6–7 kilometers from town · What people keep mentioning is the roomy, clean suites, the friendly staff, and the free private parking, which makes it a good fit for people working in the Rayong industrial estates and travelers who want a calm long stay · From around THB 990/night, average score 8.8 from real reviews

body.html: Banyan Residence overview — who it suits — The shortest way to put it: Banyan Residence Rayong is for people who want "quiet and usable space" more than buzz or a central location · It isn't a beachfront resort that puts you to sleep to the sound of waves, and it isn't a city hotel where you step out the door into a street full of restaurants · It's a 3-star serviced apartment in Noen Phra, Mueang Rayong, with rooms designed as suites — a sitting and dining area set apart from the bed — so it feels more like having your own small home than a standard hotel room · Real reviews line up on who fits here: work travelers on business or working in the Rayong industrial estates, people staying several nights in a row who want room to breathe, and families who drive themselves and value peace and quiet · On the flip side, if you're after a place by the sea you can walk down to the beach from, or a lively nightlife scene you can stroll all evening, this may not be the answer, because its selling point is privacy and an affordable price, not a tourist location · Put simply, it plays the "good value and quiet" card well on a low-thousands budget, in exchange for having a car or being willing to call one whenever you head out

Location and getting around — Banyan Residence is in Noen Phra subdistrict, Mueang Rayong, which is a residential, semi-suburban area rather than the city center · Downtown Rayong is around 6–7 kilometers away, about a 10–15 minute drive, while U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is around 37 kilometers, or roughly a 45–50 min drive, which is handy if you fly in and rent a car or have your own · The honest point is that this location is "easy to find but not walkable" — several reviews say the property sits on a main road and isn't hard to spot, but there's no convenience store, restaurant, or street food within walking distance, so you have to drive or call a ride · The good news is the property runs a free shuttle to a nearby market, which many guests praise as a real help for those without a car · If you want to sightsee, Mae Ramphueng Beach and the beaches in town are a short drive away, and if you're carrying on to Ban Phe and Koh Samet, Noen Phra works as a starting point · Bottom line: this location suits people with a car first and foremost; without one, you'll need to plan your transport and make good use of the property's shuttle

"The room was clean and bigger than expected, with a separate sitting area like a little suite. The staff were so lovely and helped with everything we asked · The only thing is there's nothing around the place, so you have to drive out to eat, but they have a free shuttle to the market so it's fine."

Room types and decor — What sets Banyan Residence apart from similarly priced hotels is that almost all the rooms are suites with a sitting and dining area set apart from the bed · It starts with the Queen Suite, a non-smoking room with one queen bed, good for couples or solo travelers who want plenty of space · Step up to the Executive Suite, which has a queen bed plus an extra sofa bed for more occupancy · And the largest is the Family Suite, with a single bed, a king bed, and a sofa bed, suited to families or groups of friends traveling together · The decor is simple and warm, leaning on wood or wood-look flooring and easy-on-the-eye tones, looking clean and tidy · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge, kettle, safe, work desk, flat-screen TV, wardrobe, and a private balcony/terrace, plus an en-suite bathroom with a hairdryer · Real reviews agree that the rooms are clean, the furniture looks new, and the space is roomy for the price, especially for guests staying multiple nights, who'll appreciate the comfort of a separate sitting area · One thing some guests note is that the mattress is fairly firm, and the bathroom and kitchenette are smaller than expected, with limited cooking equipment, so it's not a room for serious cooking every meal, but it's fine for reheating food or making drinks · If you're sensitive to mattress softness, it's worth asking for extra pillows or a mattress topper

Facilities — Since it's a compact serviced apartment, Banyan Residence's facilities focus on day-to-day essentials rather than luxury-resort amenities · The most praised feature is the free private parking on the property — no need to book ahead, easy to park, and a real advantage for self-drivers · Next is the free Wi-Fi throughout, which some reviews say works well and stays stable, though a few note the signal caps the number of users and the speed isn't very high, so if you have online meetings or heavy uploads, keep a mobile data backup ready · There's also a gym, a 24-hour front desk, luggage storage, and a lift · The service highlight many guests appreciate is the free shuttle to the market and nearby spots, which makes up nicely for the lack of shops within walking distance · To be straight about it, there is no swimming pool and no breakfast service (no breakfast), so if you're expecting a pool or a breakfast buffet at the hotel, this won't match that expectation — but if you see it as an apartment-style stay focused on good, quiet rooms, what's on offer is about right for the price

On food — This needs to be clear so no one expects the wrong thing: Banyan Residence has no restaurant and doesn't include breakfast in the room rate, per the booking platforms · That's normal for a serviced apartment in a residential area, designed for guests to head out for food or buy it back to eat in the room, which has a fridge and a kettle · The limitation of the location is that there are no restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance, so guests tend to drive into downtown Rayong to eat, or use the property's shuttle to the market to buy fresh produce and ready-made food to bring back · Downtown Rayong and the surrounding area have fresh seafood restaurants, noodle shops, cafes, and malls like Laemtong and Central Rayong with full food courts · For work travelers on a long stay, having a fridge in the room and a separate dining area helps a lot, because you can stock up on food and drinks and eat in the room comfortably without going out for every meal · In short, food here is "on you," but with rooms designed for real living plus the market shuttle, this limitation isn't the big problem it might seem

Service — Service is where Banyan Residence draws the densest praise in real reviews · Many guests mention the staff personally, saying they are friendly, smiling, and happy to help with anything asked, from check-in to recommending places to eat and visit, to arranging the market shuttle · Some reviews name a staff member who looked after them especially well, a good sign that the service comes from genuine care rather than just doing the job · The front desk is open 24 hours, so people arriving late or finishing work in the evening can check in with ease · The straightforward note is that staff with fluent English are limited, so some international guests say they had to use a translation app at times, but the team's willingness to help makes up for much of that · Overall, the warm, homey service is the charm that has many guests saying they'd come back again

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Pulled together from several booking platforms — Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor — the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: clean, roomy suites with a separate sitting area, furniture that looks new and tidy, friendly and very helpful staff, convenient free private parking, a quiet atmosphere good for resting and working, and value for money in the low-thousands range · On the gripes side: the most talked-about issue is the location with nothing within walking distance, so you need a car or a ride to go eat and shop · Next is the fairly firm mattress for some, Wi-Fi that caps users and isn't very fast at times, a bathroom and kitchenette smaller than expected, few TV channels, and no breakfast or pool · Most of these gripes can be managed by setting your expectations to match the type of stay — see it as a quiet, well-priced apartment, not a full-blown resort hotel — and the experience fits together much better

"Stayed several nights for work. The room was clean and quiet, slept well, and parking was easy with no fighting for a spot · One small gripe is the internet was slow when a lot of people were on it, and the mattress was a bit firm for us — next time I'll ask for an extra pillow."

Price and value — Banyan Residence's starting price is around THB 990/night in the normal range (some international reviews quote around 28–30 dollars a night, which is close), and it may tick up a little over long holidays or festivals · Larger rooms like the Executive Suite and Family Suite run higher, scaling with size and bed count · Compared with similarly priced hotels in Rayong, where Banyan Residence comes out ahead is that you get a suite-sized room with a sitting area and a fridge for the same price as a standard room at a typical hotel, plus free parking and peace and quiet · What you trade is a location far from shops and the lack of a pool and breakfast · For work travelers on a long stay, travelers with a car, and families who value quiet and usable space, this price is great value, because you pay for a small room but get the space of a suite · But if you prioritize a walkable location for sightseeing or want a full set of resort facilities, the same budget might find options in town that fit your needs better

Good to know before you book — A few things make the stay go more smoothly · One, sort out your transport — if you don't have your own car, ask about the schedule and terms of the property's market shuttle ahead of time, and download a ride-hailing app just in case · Two, if you're sensitive to mattress softness, ask for extra pillows or bedding at check-in, since many reviews say the mattress is fairly firm · Three, if you'll be working online for real, prepare a backup mobile data package, because the Wi-Fi can be slow when a lot of people are on it · Four, there's no breakfast and no pool here, so plan your own breakfast (the in-room fridge helps) and don't expect resort-style facilities · Five, this is a small property in a residential area with a limited number of rooms, and it can fill up fast during events or seminars at the industrial estates, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation rate first if your plans aren't firm

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Banyan Residence Rayong is the best fit for people who want a clean, roomy suite, peace and quiet, and free parking on a low-thousands budget · Rooms with a separate sitting area, a fridge, and a balcony, plus friendly staff and the market shuttle, make it good value for work travelers, long-stay guests, and families who drive themselves · But you have to accept, honestly, that the location is in a residential area away from town with no shops within walking distance, the mattress is fairly firm, and there's no pool or breakfast · If you're looking for a place by the sea you can walk down to, or a central location you can stroll and sightsee from, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a hotel in town or a resort along Mae Ramphueng Beach instead · But for a trip that values quiet, usable space, and value — and where you're fine having a car or using the property's shuttle — Banyan Residence does its job better than its price suggests, and pleasingly so

faq.q: Where is Banyan Residence Rayong · is it easy to get to?
faq.a: The property is in Noen Phra subdistrict, Mueang Rayong, in a quiet residential area, around 6–7 kilometers from downtown Rayong (a 10–15 min drive) and around 37 kilometers from U-Tapao Airport · It's easy to find since it's on a main road, but there are no shops within walking distance, so it suits people with a car or those who use the property's market shuttle

faq.q: What's the starting price at Banyan Residence · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 990/night for a Queen Suite in the normal range · There are several suite sizes: Queen Suite (queen bed), Executive Suite (queen + sofa bed), and Family Suite (single + king + sofa bed) for families · Every room has a separate sitting area, a fridge, and a balcony

faq.q: Who is Banyan Residence good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for work travelers in the industrial estates, people staying multiple nights, and families who drive themselves and value quiet · You get a roomy suite with free parking on a low-thousands budget · If you're looking for a place by the sea or a central, walkable location, a hotel in town or by the beach may suit you better

faq.q: Does Banyan Residence have breakfast and a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's no breakfast and no swimming pool, per the booking platforms · But every room has a fridge and kettle, so it's easy to buy food to eat in the room, and there's a gym, free parking, free Wi-Fi, and a 24-hour front desk · The property also runs a free shuttle to a nearby market

faq.q: What are the mattress and Wi-Fi like at Banyan Residence?
faq.a: Many reviews say the mattress is fairly firm, so if you like it soft, it's worth asking for extra pillows or bedding at check-in · As for the Wi-Fi, it's free but at times caps users and isn't very fast, so if you have online meetings or heavy uploads, prepare a backup mobile data package

faq.q: Where can you go from Banyan Residence?
faq.a: Use it as a base to drive into downtown Rayong for seafood and shopping at Laemtong/Central malls in 10–15 minutes · Mae Ramphueng Beach is a short drive away, and if you're heading on to Ban Phe to catch a boat to Koh Samet, Noen Phra works as a convenient starting point
